content.thinking:
I need to avoid restating the impact figures as if I calculated them myself, since those numbers came from the shop's own accounting, not my analysis. I should focus the postmortem on qualitative description and timestamps for onset and recovery rather than quoting cost figures as my own computation.

For the executive summary, I want to note the timeframe (23:41 to 23:47 UTC) as given facts, describe the error rate rise qualitatively, and list assumptions like the restart being correlated but not proven causal, unknown root cause for the pricing service slowness, and no deploy/flag changes in the window. The root cause centers on the internal pricing service responding slowly on basket-total calls, with checkout latency rising in lockstep and no local config change detected.

assumptions: Causation between the restart and the recovery is inferred from timing only: io-pricing was restarted at 23:46:43 and io-shop was observed at baseline at 23:47:05. It was not proven that the restart, rather than the condition clearing on its own, ended the incident.

io-pricing is treated as an internally owned dependency (checkout-platform) on the strength of the service register. If that ownership record is stale and the service is in fact run by a third party, this is an upstream-dependency failure instead, and the remediation path changes.

The absence of a trigger is based on a bounded search: production change events for io-shop over the 166 minutes before the alert and the feature-flag provider's recent history. Changes outside those windows, or changes made to io-pricing itself, were not checked.

The ClientDisconnected errors on the account page appear in the logs from 23:38, before the onset at 23:41, and continue at a similar rate afterwards. They are assumed to be background noise unrelated to the latency, not a symptom of it - this was not verified.
The 1500ms figure is taken from the log lines as emitted; no independent measurement of io-pricing's own latency was made from io-pricing's side.
The incident is assumed fully resolved rather than temporarily masked. Since the reason io-pricing degraded is unknown, a recurrence after the restart cannot be ruled out.
The draft pull request opened at 23:51 has not been reviewed or merged and is not assumed to address the root cause in io-pricing.
input.executive_summary: Late on 25 September the online shop got slow for shoppers. Pages that need a basket total - the account and checkout pages - took roughly a second and a half longer than usual to come back, and a small share of requests failed that normally would have succeeded. The slowness began at 23:41 UTC and the service was back to its normal behaviour by 23:47 UTC. The cause was not the shop itself but an internal pricing service it calls to work out basket totals, which started answering very slowly. Our automated responder picked up the alert, traced the delay to that pricing service, restarted it, and confirmed the shop had returned to normal. A draft code change has since been opened for review to make the shop more resilient when that dependency is slow. Shoppers who were browsing during the affected minutes saw slow pages and, in a small number of cases, a page that did not load; no data was lost or incorrectly priced as far as the logs show.
input.root_cause: An internal dependency, io-pricing (pricing.io-internal.svc, owned by checkout-platform), began taking about 1500ms to answer io-shop's /v1/shoppers/.../basket-total calls at the onset, and io-shop's p50/p95/p99 moved in lockstep with it (~45/220/380ms to ~1545/1720/1870ms); no deploy, config, or feature-flag change was found on io-shop in the window queried, so the latency arrived through the dependency rather than originating in io-shop. Why io-pricing slowed down was not established - a restart of it cleared the symptom, but the underlying trigger in that service is still unknown.
